šubultum: consignment, goods sent for carriage (Harper: “goods for transportation”): šibultim (ši-bu-ul-tim) in bēl šibultim “the owner of the consignment”, ana šibultim “as a consignment”
našpakum: bin, store for grain (Harper: “heap, bin”): našpakam, našpakim (na-aš-pa-kam, na-aš-pa-ki-im; the last syllable of -kam is the sign KAM), ina našpakim “from the bin”
maškanum: storehouse, granary (Harper: “granary, storage-house”): maškanim (ma-aš-ka-nim) “of/in the storehouse”; also written with two Sumerogram signs KI.UD, which Harper’s glossary names KISLAḪ for maškanum; the identification of the pair is checked only on the plate, UNCERTAIN
nibūtum: hostage for debt, a person taken as pledge (Harper: “hostage”; from nebûm; later dictionaries write nipûtum, with p, from nepûm): nibūtum, nibūtim; nibūssu (ni-bu-zu, the sign ZU standing for -ssu, nibūt + -šu) “his hostage”; ana nibūtim “for a hostage”
nebûm: to distrain, seize as a pledge (Harper; later dictionaries write nepûm, with p): ittebi (it-te-bi, perfect) “he has distrained”; ibbima (ib-bi-ma, preterite + -ma) “he distrained, and” (Harper lists ib-bi under this verb); nēbīša (ne-bi-ša) “her distrainer”, the one who holds the hostage (a noun from the verb, with -ša; the exact shape of the noun is UNCERTAIN)
1/3: one third — a fraction sign, ⅓ MA.NA kaspim “a third of a mina of silver”; the spoken form šalšāt (?) is reconstructed, and the identification of the fraction sign is UNCERTAIN (the character used is only the nearest Unicode sign)
mâtum: to die: imtūt (im-tu-ut, perfect) “he/she has died”, so ina šīmātīša imtūt “she died a natural death”
kiššātum: service, being held in service for a debt (Harper: kiššatu “service”; a different word from kiššatum “totality” of the prologue): kiššātim (ki-iš-ša-tim, ki-iš-ša-a-tim), ana kiššātim “into service”
andurārum: freedom, release from debt-service (Harper): andurāršunu (an-du-ra-ar-šu-nu) “their release”
etēqum-Š: Š-stem of etēqum “to pass”: to make pass, pass on: ušētiq (u-še-ti-iq, preterite) “he made (him) pass on”
baqārum-N: N-stem of baqārum (Harper BAKARU IV): to be claimed: ibbaqqar (ib-ba-qar, present) “he shall be claimed”, ul ibbaqqar “no claim shall be made”
walādum: to bear, give birth to: ūlidušum (ul-du-šum) “(whom) she bore to him” (preterite ūlid, the long ū of a w-initial verb, with the subjunctive -u and the dative -šum; Harper’s spelling is shortened, so the vowels of the form are UNCERTAIN)
padārum: to ransom, redeem (Harper): ipaddar (i-pa-dar, present) “he shall redeem”
šapākum: to heap up, store (grain): išpuk (iš-pu-uk, preterite) “he has stored”; išpukma (iš-pu-uk-ma) “he stored, and”
ibbûm: UNCERTAIN: “accident”, following Harper’s gloss: ibbûm (i-ib-bu-u-um); the word is met in only one place and the sense is taken from Harper and the context (damage with no one’s fault)
šapākum-N: N-stem of šapākum: to be stored: iššapku (iš-ša-ap-ku) “(which) was stored” (passive with the subjunctive -u)
gamrum: complete, whole (Harper: “complete, total”): gamrim (ga-am-ri-im), ana gamrim “for the whole”
5: five — the numeral 5, five wedges: 5 qa “five qa”, said ḫamšat (?) qa (spoken form reconstructed; the form before a noun is assumed)
qûm: the qa, a capacity measure of about a litre (Harper: QA), written with the sign SÌLA: ḫamšat qa šeʾim “five qa of grain”; the identification of the plate’s sign as SÌLA is the editor’s, UNCERTAIN
idum: hire, wages (Harper: ID, the ideogram for hire): idi našpakim “the hire of the bin”, written with the single sign Á (A₂, “arm; hire”); the case ending is not written, so idi (construct, before a genitive) is an assumed reading, UNCERTAIN
šalāmum-D: D-stem of šalāmum “to be whole, sound”: to make good, restore (Harper: “to restore”): ušallamma (u-ša-lam-ma) “he shall make good, and”
šarrāqānum: thief (Harper): šarrāqānišu (šar-ra-qa₂-ni-šu) “his thief”, the thief in question
babtum: UNCERTAIN: Harper’s “loss, defects”, but in §126 apparently the party accused of the loss, “the one blamed” (later dictionaries have babtum as a city quarter or ward, which would be a group held liable): babtašu, babtišu (ba-ab-ta-šu, ba-ab-ti-šu) “his babtum”; the sense is not secure
ragāmum: to claim, to call out a claim: irgumu (ir-gu-mu, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(whatever) he claimed”

__broaden__.maḫāṣum: to strike; of ground, to break up: imaḫḫaṣ “he shall break up” · the noun maḫāṣum “beating, abuse, injury” (Harper), written ma-ḫa-ṣi-im with the sign ZI (value ṣi): maḫāṣim “(through) beating”
__broaden__.šīmtum: fate; one’s natural death: ana šīmtim ittalak “he went to (his) fate” = he died · plural šīmātum “fates”: šīmātīša (ši-ma-ti-ša) “her fates”; ina šīmātīša imtūt “she died in her fates” = she died a natural death
__broaden__.iʾiltum: bond, debt-obligation: ana iʾiltišu / eḫiltišu “for his debt” · eḫiltum (e-ḫi-il-tum) “debt” as the grammatical subject, a debt that “seizes” a man: eḫiltum awīlam iṣbassuma “a debt has seized a man, and”
__broaden__.ṣabātum: to seize: iṣṣabat, ṣabtu · stative with the subjunctive -u: adi kirâm ṣabtu “as long as he holds the orchard” (with Harper’s kirûm: “as long as the orchard is held”) · iṣṣabtamma (iṣ-ṣa-ab-tam-ma) “she seized (them), and” (perfect with the ventive -am and -ma): lā iṣṣabtamma “and she did not seize” · iṣbassuma (iṣ-ba-zu-ma, ZU for -ssu) “it seized him, and” (preterite iṣbat + -šu + -ma), of a debt seizing a man
__broaden__.wašābum: to sit: ul uššab “he shall not sit” (the stone writes uš-ta-ab — a carver’s slip Harper flags) · to dwell: wāšbum (participle, contracted) “the dweller, the tenant” (a conjectured reading, aš-bu-u[m]); wa… “dwell-” in broken forms · stative wašbat (wa-aš-ba-at) “she dwells, lives”: ša ina gagîm lā wašbat “who does not live in the cloister” · stative wašib (wa-ši-ib-ma, with -ma) “he is staying”: ina ḫarrānim wašib “he is staying on the road”
__broaden__.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant” · ittadinma (it-ta-di-in-ma) “he has given, and” (perfect); inaddinu (i-na-ad-di-nu) “(which) he gives” (present, with the subjunctive -u) · ittandin (it-ta-an-di-in, perfect with an extra -n-) “he has handed over”: ana kiššātim ittandin “he handed over into service”; ittadin (it-ta-din) “he has given”, i.e. sold; ana maṣṣarūtim inaddin “he gives for safekeeping”; iddinūšumma “they gave him, and”
__broaden__.wabālum-Š: Š-stem of wabālum “to carry”: to make carry off, let (water) carry away: uštābil (perfect) “he has let (the water) carry off” · ušābilšu (u-ša-bil-šu, preterite) “he had (him) carry”; šūbulu (šu-bu-lu, Š stative šūbul with the subjunctive -u) “(what) has been sent”, šūbulūma (šu-bu-lu-ma) “has been sent, and”; the stative reading is from the form and the exact sense is UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.kânum-D: D-stem of kânum: to convict, prove against someone (uktīn, ukannūšuma) · uktīn (uk-ti-in, perfect, with the infixed -t-) “he has convicted”; ukannūšuma (u-ka-an-nu-šu-ma, present, plural, with -šu “him” and -ma) “they shall convict him, and”; ukānma (u-ka-an-ma, present, singular) “he shall convict, and”
__broaden__.ḫalāqum: to be lost, vanish: ḫalqu, ḫalqam · iḫtaliq (iḫ-ta-li-iq, perfect) “it has been lost”; ḫaliq (ḫa-li-iq, stative) “(it) is lost”, ḫaliqma “is lost, and”; lā ḫaliqma “is not lost, and”
__broaden__.tabālum: to take away, carry off: itabbal · tabal “take!” (imperative) · itbal (it-ba-al, preterite) “he took away”
__broaden__.bašûm-N: N-stem of bašûm: to be there, be found: ibbaššû (present, 3rd plural, in a ša-clause) “which are found” · ittabši (it-tab-ši, perfect) “it has come about, has happened”
__broaden__.bârum: to establish, prove; D-stem: ubârma “he shall prove (it), and…” · ubâršuma (u-ba-ar-šu-ma) “he shall prove him, and” (D present with -šu “him” and -ma; Harper’s gloss for this form is “to declare, to itemize”; who proves whom in §126 is UNCERTAIN)
__broaden__.abārum: to accuse; D-stem ubburum: ubbirma “he accused”, mubbirum “accuser” · utebbir (u-te-ib-bi-ir, Dt preterite, Harper’s stem II,2, the reflexive of the D-stem) “he has made a claim against” (Harper: “to file a claim for”)
__broaden__.egûm: to be careless, neglect (Harper: “to be careless”): itēgi(ma) “he has been negligent, and” · igûma (i-gu-ma) “(who) was careless, and” (the preterite igi with the relative -u, as ilqû beside ilqe, then -ma)
__broaden__.epēšum: to do, make: epēšim “doing” · to work (land): ippeš(ma) (present): eqlam šipram ippeš “he shall do the work on the field” · to build (?) (a house): bītam ippēšma(?) “he builds a house, and”, the verb broken; iteppuš (?) in a broken line · ippešū (i-ib-bi-šu) “they shall do (work), they shall work” (present plural)
__broaden__.šattum: year: šattam (syllabic, §31) or MU (the year-sign, §30) · šattim (genitive); plural šanātim “years” (ša šanātim “of the years”); MU 4{kam}, said erbe šanātim “four years” · MU 3{kam}, said šalāš šanātim “for three years”; šanat (ša-na-at) “(in) the year”, ina šanat “each year”
__broaden__.mārum: son (DUMU) — here: a minor, not yet able to sell · member of a group: mārū ugārim (DUMU A.GÀR{meš}) “the sons of the irrigated land”, the district’s farmers · mār awīlim “a man’s son” (DUMU); mārī (DUMU{meš}) “sons” (oblique plural, which may include daughters, so “children”); māršu (DUMU-šu) “his son”
__broaden__.mārtum: daughter (written DUMU+ti): mārtišu “his daughter” · mārassu (DUMU.SAL-zu, three signs DUMU + SAL + ZU, ZU for -ssu) “his daughter”
__broaden__.aššatum: wife: ana aššatišu “to his wife” · aššassu (SAL-zu, ZU for -ssu) “his wife”
__broaden__.wardum: male slave (ARAD) · warad (ARAD, no ending written) “male slave of …”, wardam (ARAD-am)
__broaden__.kurrum: the kor, a grain measure (written GUR; Harper: 300 KA): kur šeʾam “a kor of grain” · written GUR.É (the editors’ print GUR-É) as well as GUR: 1 GUR.É, kurrum “a kor” (UNCERTAIN: the .É is not explained here) · written ŠE.GUR.E, with a final E: ana 1 ŠE.GUR.E “for one kor (of grain)”; the .E is not explained here, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.qātum: hand: ina qāt “from the hand of” · qātīšu (qa₂-ti-šu) “of his hands”: bīš qātīšu “his own goods”
__broaden__.bīšum: movable property, goods, possessions: bīšašu “his goods” · short construct form bīš (bi-iš) before a genitive: bīš qātīšu “his own goods”
__broaden__.dâkum: to kill; N-stem iddâk “he shall be killed” — the code’s death sentence · idukkū (i-du-uk-ku) “they shall kill” (active plural, unlike the N-stem iddâk)
__broaden__.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule” · “since, when”, before a stative: kīma mimmûšu lā ḫalqu “since his goods are not lost”
__broaden__.itti: with · “from”, after leqûm “to take”: itti šarrāqānišu ileqqi “from his thief he shall take”
__broaden__.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year”
__broaden__.nakārum: UNCERTAIN: perhaps nakārum “to be hostile, to deny, to dispute”: only the first sign ik survives, which the editor doubts, so the form (ikkir-ma ?) and the sense are a guess; the verb is the editors’ restoration · ittakir (it-ta-ki-ir, perfect) “he denied, disowned (his merchant)”, ittakiršu “he denied him”, ikkiru (ik-ki-ru, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(because) he denied”: here the forms are spelled out on the stele, so the verb nakārum is sure; Harper’s heading is “to be different, to be hostile, to dispute” · ittakir (it-ta-ki-ir, perfect) “he denied” a deposit: ana gamrim ittakir “he denied it altogether”; ittakiršu (it-ta-ki-ir-šu) “he has denied him”; ittakrūšu (it-ta-ak-ru-šu, perfect, plural, with -šu) “they have denied him”; ikkiru (ik-ki-ru, preterite with the subjunctive -u) “(whatever) he denied”: the verb is spelled out on the stele in these laws, so nakārum “to deny” is sure here
__broaden__.mimmûm: property, belongings: mimmûšu “his property” · mimmâšu (mi-im-ma-šu, accusative) “his goods”; mimmûšu (mi-im-mu-šu) “his goods” as subject; mimmê (mi-im-me-e, oblique): itti mimmê bēl bītim “with the goods of the owner of the house”; mimmēšu (mi-im-me-šu, oblique-looking, bracketed by Harper) “his goods”
__broaden__.nabalkattum: UNCERTAIN: apparently “crossing-over”, a noun from the root BLKT of nabalkutum “to cross over”; nabalkatka “your crossing-over (?)”; the sense is a guess, and the word is broken in places (naba…, …katim) · nabalkattim (na-ba-al-ka-at-tim, split by the stone over two lines) after ina, beside ina pilšim “through a breach”: a second way into a house, read “by crossing-over (the wall)”; Harper’s glossary has “pillage”; the sense stays UNCERTAIN

kalāmum-D: D-stem of kalāmum (Harper: KALAMU, “to show, inform”): to show: ukallam (u-kal-lam, present) “he shall show”
šeʾûm-Gtn: Gtn-stem (repeated action) of šeʾûm “to seek” (Harper: “to search for”): ištenēʾima (iš-te-ne-i-ma, present, with the infix -ten-) “he shall search about, and”; the stem analysis is from the form, UNCERTAIN
našpakūtum: storage, being stored: the abstract in -ūtum built on našpakum “bin”: ana našpakūtim (na-aš-pa-ku-tim) “for storage”, as maṣṣarūtum is “safekeeping”
